sentences.text:
In the frozen Arctic tundra, engineers spent
24 years drilling the *deepest hole on Earth*.
sentences.spoken: In the frozen Arctic tundra of the Kola Peninsula, Soviet engineers spent twenty-four years drilling the deepest artificial hole on Earth.

sentences.text:
Reaching *12,262 meters down*,
the drill went 7 miles into Earth's crust.
sentences.spoken: Reaching twelve thousand two hundred and sixty-two meters down, the drill penetrated more than seven miles into the continental crust.

sentences.text:
At 7 kilometers down, they found fractured rock
saturated with *boiling hydrothermal water*.
sentences.spoken: At seven kilometers down, geologists expected dense dry granite, but instead found fractured rock saturated with boiling water.

sentences.text:
Trapped *hydrogen gas boiled out*
in quantities that stunned geologists.
sentences.spoken: Trapped hydrogen gas boiled out of the mud in quantities that stunned the Soviet science academy.

sentences.text:
They found *microscopic plankton fossils*
preserved in 2-billion-year-old rock.
sentences.spoken: Even more astonishing, they discovered microscopic plankton fossils six kilometers deep, perfectly preserved in two billion year old rock.

sentences.text:
Temperatures soared to *180°C*,
turning ancient granite into soft plastic.
sentences.spoken: By twelve kilometers, subterranean temperatures soared to one hundred and eighty degrees Celsius, turning rock into ductile plastic.

sentences.text:
The softened rock flowed like putty,
*destroying drill bits within minutes*.
sentences.spoken: The rock behaved like putty, flowing back into the drill shaft and destroying cutting heads within minutes.

sentences.text:
Urban legends claimed 'screaming souls',
but sensors recorded *tectonic acoustic stress*.
sentences.spoken: Sensational rumors claimed microphones recorded screaming souls, but the real telemetry revealed acoustic pressure waves of shifting tectonic stress.

sentences.text:
Today, that nine-inch portal sits
*welded shut beneath a rusty steel cap*.
sentences.spoken: Today, that nine-inch portal into the underworld sits welded shut beneath a rusty steel cap, an abandoned gateway to the abyss.
